mainTopic: Can a קרבן animal with קדושת הגוף become חולין? רבי מאיר (במזיד, by intent) versus רבי יהודה, and the extension to קדשים קלים.
overview: The גמרא quotes a משנה in שקלים about a stray animal found near ירושלים: males are treated as עולות and females as שלמים. It asks why a male could not also be a שלמים. רבי אושעיא answers that the finder redeems the animal by paying its value, and the money must cover both possibilities. This works according to רבי מאיר, who holds that הקדש becomes חולין when it is misused on purpose (במזיד). The גמרא challenges this from a משנה in מעילה showing that things with קדושת הגוף never lose their holiness, and it answers that that משנה follows רבי יהודה. The גמרא then asks why רבי מאיר does not also keep קדושת הגוף holy, as רבי יהודה does. It answers that someone who acts on purpose actually intends to make the item חולין. Finally, רבי יעקב uses a קל וחומר to show that רבי מאיר's rule covers קדשים קלים too, and a statement in רבי מאיר's name confirms it.

steps.title: The stray animal found near ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in שקלים: an animal found between ירושלים and מגדל עדר, or the same distance in any direction, is assumed to be a קרבן. Males are treated as עולות and females as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: if an animal is found anywhere from ירושלים out to מגדל עדר, or that same distance in any direction, the males are treated as burnt-offerings and the females as peace-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכת (שקלים) as the base text for the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals near ירושלים most likely came from the city, where most animals were set aside for קרבנות. So the משנה assumes a stray animal there is a קרבן. A male is called an עולה because only males can be עולות, and a female is called a שלמים because females are allowed for שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה there (in another מסכת)
A place near ירושלים, used here as a distance marker
Burnt-offerings, which must be male
Peace-offerings, which may be male or female

phrases.english: We learned there:
An animal that was found
from Jerusalem to Migdal Eder
and within that same distance in every direction,
males are burnt-offerings,
females are peace-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the sugya with a base text quoted from שקלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stray animal found near ירושלים is assumed to be a קרבן: males are עולות and females are שלמים.

steps.title: Why can't a male be a peace-offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a male animal could just as easily be a שלמים, so why does the משנה treat males only as עולות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But are males only burnt-offerings and not peace-offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule for males, because males are also allowed as שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female can only be a שלמים, so that part of the rule makes sense. A male, however, could have been set aside as either an עולה or a שלמים. The משנה's simple label of "עולות" seems to ignore that possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: But (opening a challenge)
They are

phrases.english: But males —
is it only burnt-offerings that they are,
and not peace-offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling for males in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that males are treated as עולות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Males can also be שלמים, so labeling them only as עולות seems incomplete.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: the finder pays the value, following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains that the משנה is not about offering the animal itself. It is about a finder who redeems the animal by paying its value. For a male we worry it might be an עולה, so the money must cover both possibilities. This follows רבי מאיר, who holds that הקדש becomes חולין when misused במזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: here we are dealing with someone who comes to obligate himself in the animals' value. This is what the משנה means: we are concerned that the males might be burnt-offerings. And it follows רבי מאיר, who says that consecrated property loses its holiness when it is misused on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers the question by changing the case: the finder pays for the animal instead of offering it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not mean that males are definitely עולות. It means we must also consider that they might be עולות, so the money is used for both an עולה and a שלמים. For the animal to lose its holiness through this redemption, the משנה must follow רבי מאיר's view that הקדש becomes חולין when this is done deliberately.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes to take on an obligation to pay their value
We are dealing with
We are concerned (about a possibility)
Property that has been made holy
On purpose, deliberately
Loses its holiness and becomes ordinary (חולין)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה's word "עולות" does not mean the male definitely is an עולה. According to רבי אושעיא, it means we must also take into account that it might be one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
Here, with one who comes to obligate himself
in their value we are dealing,
phrases.notes: The finder pays the animal's worth to the הקדש so that he may keep the animal itself.

phrases.english: and this is what it is saying:
we are concerned that perhaps they are burnt-offerings,
and it follows Rabbi Meir,
who said: consecrated property is desacralized when misused intentionally.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: הָכָא בָּבָא לָחוּב בִּדְמֵיהֶן עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by redefining the case and naming the תנא it follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) and attributing the משנה to רבי מאיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that males are definitely offered as עולות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The finder redeems the animal. For males we also consider the possibility of an עולה, which works according to רבי מאיר's view that הקדש becomes חולין when misused במזיד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer depends on the animal being able to lose its holiness, which sets up the next challenge.

steps.title: Can something with inherent holiness be redeemed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא: an animal set aside as a קרבן has קדושת הגוף. A משנה in מעילה teaches that such an animal, like a כלי שרת, never loses its holiness. Each new person who uses it commits מעילה again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can something with inherent holiness lose its holiness? But we learned: there is no misuse after misuse with holy things, except for an animal and a service vessel. How so? If one person was riding on a holy animal, another came and rode, and another came and rode, they all committed מעילה. If one was drinking from a gold cup of the מקדש, another came and drank, and another came and drank, they all committed מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אושעיא's answer using a משנה that shows a קרבן animal can never become חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With most holy items, the first person who misuses them makes them חולין, so later users commit no מעילה. A קרבן animal and a כלי שרת are different: every user commits מעילה, which shows they stay holy. If so, how can the animal in the שקלים case be redeemed?

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness of the item itself, not just of its value
But didn't we learn in a משנה (a challenge)
One who commits מעילה, misusing holy property
A vessel used in the מקדש service
How so? (introduces examples)
They committed מעילה

steps.confusionAlert: "אין מועל אחר מועל" means that after one person's misuse, a second person's use is no longer מעילה. The exception means the animal and the vessel stay holy no matter how many people misuse them.

phrases.english: And can inherent sanctity be desacralized?
But didn't we learn:
There is no misuse after misuse with consecrated items
except with an animal and a service vessel alone.
How so?
If one was riding on an animal,
another came and rode,
another came and rode —
they have all committed misuse.
If one was drinking from a golden cup,
another came and drank,
another came and drank —
they have all committed misuse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in רבי אושעיא's answer that the animal can lose its holiness.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's claim that the stray קרבן animal can be redeemed and become חולין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in מעילה shows that animals and כלי שרת, which have קדושת הגוף, never lose their holiness even through misuse.

steps.title: Two משניות, two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה in מעילה follows רבי יהודה, while the משנה in שקלים follows רבי מאיר, who holds that even הקדש with קדושת הגוף can become חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That משנה follows רבי יהודה; this one follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each משנה to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two משניות do not have to agree because they follow different opinions. According to רבי יהודה, קדושת הגוף cannot be removed by misuse. According to רבי מאיר, it can, so רבי אושעיא's explanation of the שקלים case holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (the other source)
This one (the source we started with)
The תנא who holds that קדושת הגוף is never removed

steps.whatToRemember: The stray-animal משנה follows רבי מאיר: holy property, even with קדושת הגוף, becomes חולין when misused במזיד. The משנה in מעילה follows רבי יהודה, who disagrees.

phrases.english: That one follows Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the משנה in מעילה about riding and drinking.

phrases.english: this one follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by attributing the two משניות to different תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in מעילה seemed to be a universal rule that קדושת הגוף never lapses.
steps.terutzMaskana: That rule follows only רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר holds that it can lapse, and the שקלים משנה follows him.

steps.title: Should רבי מאיר agree with רבי יהודה about inherent holiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי מאיר should follow רבי יהודה's pattern. Even if regular הקדש can become חולין, an item with קדושת הגוף should stay holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn רבי מאיר's view from רבי יהודה's view. רבי יהודה says regular הקדש becomes חולין when misused by mistake, but קדושת הגוף does not. So רבי מאיר should say the same: regular הקדש becomes חולין when misused on purpose, but קדושת הגוף should not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 5 by comparing רבי מאיר to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה draws a line: regular הקדש can lose its holiness, but קדושת הגוף cannot. The גמרא suggests רבי מאיר should draw the same line. If he does, a found animal with קדושת הגוף could never be redeemed, and רבי אושעיא's explanation falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: By mistake, without knowing
Let us learn, let us infer
Does not lose its holiness (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: From Rabbi Yehuda let us learn about Rabbi Meir:
Didn't Rabbi Yehuda say:
consecrated property becomes non-sacred when misused by mistake,
but inherent holiness does not become non-sacred.
According to Rabbi Meir as well,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּמֵזִיד מִתְחַלֵּל
phrases.english: even though consecrated property becomes non-sacred when misused on purpose,
inherent holiness should not become non-sacred!
phrases.notes: This is the problem: the found animal in the משנה has this kind of holiness, so it could not be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 5 by comparing רבי מאיר to רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that רבי מאיר lets קדושת הגוף become חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה separates regular הקדש from קדושת הגוף, so רבי מאיר should make the same split. Then a found animal could not be redeemed.

steps.title: Acting on purpose means intending to make it חולין
steps.stepSummary: Someone who misuses הקדש by mistake has no plan to remove its holiness. Someone who acts on purpose does mean to make it חולין, so for רבי מאיר even קדושת הגוף can be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in רבי יהודה's case, the person does not mean to make the items חולין. Here, in רבי מאיר's case, he does mean to make them חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are not alike, because the person's intention is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who acts בשוגג is only using the item. He never tries to remove its holiness, so קדושת הגוף stays. Someone who acts במזיד is deliberately trying to turn it into חולין, and for רבי מאיר that intention works even on קדושת הגוף.

keyTerms.meaning: Intends, means to do
To take them out of holiness
Non-holy, ordinary status

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up who holds what. רבי יהודה's rule is about acting by mistake, and רבי מאיר's rule is about acting on purpose. The answer works because of exactly this difference.

phrases.english: There, he does not intend
phrases.notes: "There" means רבי יהודה's case, where the person acted by mistake.

phrases.english: to take them out to non-sacred status.
Here, he does intend
to take them out to non-sacred status.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא קָא מְכַוֵּין לְאַפּוֹקִינְהוּ לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the comparison raised in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases, based on the person's intention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר should split regular הקדש from קדושת הגוף, just like רבי יהודה
steps.terutzMaskana: Acting on purpose means deliberately making the item חולין, and that can remove even קדושת הגוף

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר's rule apply to קדשים קלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר's rule covers only קדשי קדשים, or also קדשים קלים such as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe you heard רבי מאיר say this about קדשי קדשים. But did you hear him say it about קדשים קלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with רבי אושעיא's explanation: maybe רבי מאיר's rule covers only the holiest קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is קדשי קדשים, but a שלמים is קדשים קלים. In רבי אושעיא's explanation, the found animal might be a שלמים. If רבי מאיר lets only קדשי קדשים be redeemed, that explanation does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: קרבנות of the highest holiness, such as an עולה
קרבנות of lesser holiness, such as a שלמים
Say, perhaps

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Meir hold this
regarding offerings of the most sacred order,
but regarding offerings of lesser sanctity, did you hear him say it?
phrases.notes: This matters because the found animal might be a שלמים, and a שלמים is one of the קדשים קלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּקׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 7 and raises a new limit on רבי מאיר's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's use of רבי מאיר for an animal that might be a שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Perhaps רבי מאיר allows redeeming only קדשי קדשים. A possible שלמים would then stay holy.

steps.title: רבי יעקב answers with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב argues that if the holier קרבנות can become חולין, the less holy ones certainly can.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages, named רבי יעקב, answered: it is a קל וחומר. If קדשי קדשים can become חולין, then surely קדשים קלים can too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב answers the question of step 8 with simple logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something holier is harder to make חולין. So if רבי מאיר lets even קדשי קדשים lose their holiness, קדשים קלים must be able to lose it as well. That means a found שלמים can be redeemed too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one: if it is true here, it is surely true there
All the more so
A certain one of the Sages

phrases.english: A certain one of the Sages said to him,
and his name was Rabbi Yaakov:
It is an a fortiori inference:
If offerings of the most sacred order can become non-sacred,
is it not all the more so for offerings of lesser sanctity?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שְׁמֵיהּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר from the stronger case to the weaker one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's rule might be limited to קדשי קדשים
steps.terutzMaskana: If the holier קרבנות can become חולין, the less holy ones surely can

steps.title: A statement in רבי מאיר's name confirms the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: A statement passed down in רבי מאיר's name says the same thing. הקדש becomes חולין when misused on purpose but not by mistake, and this applies to both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, using the same קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חמא son of רבי עקיבא said in the name of רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא that רבי מאיר used to say: הקדש misused on purpose becomes חולין, and misused by mistake does not. This applies to both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, by a קל וחומר: if קדשי קדשים can become חולין, surely קדשים קלים can too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement passed down in רבי מאיר's name that supports רבי יעקב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This statement confirms that רבי מאיר himself applied his rule to קדשים קלים, and for the same reason רבי יעקב gave. It also says clearly that misuse by mistake does not make הקדש חולין for רבי מאיר. With this, רבי אושעיא's explanation of the משנה in שקלים fully stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, introducing a supporting statement
He used to say
Both this and that

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, misusing הקדש on purpose makes it חולין, even with קדושת הגוף and even for קדשים קלים, because the person means to make it חולין. That is why the finder in the משנה in שקלים can redeem the animal and cover both possibilities.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the defense of רבי אושעיא, so the משנה in שקלים can be explained according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Akiva said
that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Rabbi Meir used to say:
Consecrated property misused on purpose becomes non-sacred;
misused by mistake, it does not become non-sacred.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים וְאֶחָד קֳדָשִׁים קַלִּים.
phrases.english: This applies both to offerings of the most sacred order and to offerings of lesser sanctity.
By an a fortiori inference:
If offerings of the most sacred order can become non-sacred,
is it not all the more so for offerings of lesser sanctity?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יעקב's קל וחומר from step 9 with a statement in רבי מאיר's name
steps.raayaObject: רבי יעקב's claim that רבי מאיר's rule covers קדשים קלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement from רבי חמא son of רבי עקיבא, in the name of רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא, quoting רבי מאיר
